mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified inflation spike.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS employment exceeds 10,000 jobs, accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE, signals labor market strengthening that drives S&P 500 forward returns positive over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 10,000 AND UNRATE < previous month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the labor signal (Spearman's rho < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 industrial production of at least 2% followed by a rebound above prior trend predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as market anticipates demand recovery.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 drops 2% in two consecutive months then rises above prior 12-month trend
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative during the identified rebound period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO supply index above 2% for three months indicates supply-side expansion, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days due to profit-erasing expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month + 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the supply expansion window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 4% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 20 days due to higher real borrowing costs compressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the high-rate period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 3% combined with a decline in HOUST housing starts predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as weak labor and housing signals boost risk appetite.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the combined labor-housing signal (Spearman's rho < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly RSAFS demand reading falling by more than 5% from the prior month, without a compensating rise in FEDFUNDS, predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as a demand shock is interpreted as recessionary.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < previous month - 5% AND FEDFUNDS <= previous month
regime_hint: demand shock in tight policy environment
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified shock period.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE rises above 5% for three consecutive months in a low-inflation regime, S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days are expected to be negative due to higher wage growth depressing real business profits.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% for three consecutive months AND regime: low inflation
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or not statistically different from zero during the high UNRATE period (p > 0.05).
